section.sectionSummaryBrief: From the fact that in souls the aspect of "face" extends also into the aspect of "back," it follows that in Torah as well, the "face" of Torah illuminates its "back," which is explained through four levels of Torah: inheritance, gift, self-preparation, and bride.
section.t: And behold, from this that in the souls there is drawn from the aspect of "face" also into the aspect of "back"
(as explained above at length)
it is understood that also in the Torah
[for He looked into the Torah and created the world]
the aspect of "face" of Torah illuminates the aspect of "back" within it.
And this will be understood by what is explained by the Rebbe Maharash in the continuation "Vechocho" 5637
[for this year is the centennial year of its utterance]
that in the Torah there are four aspects.
For it is written,
"Torah tzivah lanu Moshe morashah..." that the Torah was given to us as an inheritance,
for the word "morashah" is also a term of inheritance,
and seemingly, did not our Sages say,
"Prepare yourself to study Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you,"
and this is the opposite of the exposition of "morashah" as a term of inheritance,
and sometimes we find in the words of our Sages
that the Torah was given to us as a gift, and sometimes we find that the Torah is called a bride, according to the exposition of our Sages
[on the verse "Torah tzivah lanu..."]
"Do not read 'morashah' but 'me'orasah,' that the Torah is a bride betrothed to a man, they are the souls of Israel, etc."

And behold, all these four aspects are matters and subjects different from each other, for the matter of inheritance is something that comes by necessity, for any condition that contradicts what is written in the Torah is void,
for the commandment of inheritance is by necessity, etc.
And the matter of a gift is according to the will of the giver, for if the giver wishes to give the gift, it is good, and if not, it is not at all the recipient's,
and the matter of "prepare yourself" is specifically through effort, that when one works well,
then the quality of his work which he worked in will come to him, and when the work is not so, he does not have it,
and this is what it urges, saying "prepare yourself to study," because it is not an inheritance that comes by necessity,
and it is also not a gift that is given even if one did not work so much,
but rather "prepare yourself" to toil yourself in the study of Torah, for through this you will succeed, etc.
And the matter of the Torah being called a bride is also a different matter, etc.
And the explanation is,
behold, the fulfillment of Torah is impossible except through immense toil, etc., as our Sages said,
"If you have toiled and found, believe;
if you have not toiled and found, do not believe," for without toil it is impossible to find words of Torah,

and like the statement "prepare yourself to study Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you," lest you say it will come even without any toil at all, etc. And according to the work that one works in the study of Torah, accordingly he will grow in understanding of Torah and the drawing down of Divinity that is drawn through his study and toil in Torah, etc. And about this our Sages said,
"Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him," that he draws down a drawing of Divinity in Torah,

and in this aspect of drawing down, the souls of Israel are called a groom and the Torah is called a bride, etc. And that the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews is specifically "opposite him,"
meaning, through the fact that the person reads and reviews.
And the matter of inheritance and gift is,
behold, all the matter of the performance of the commandments
[for greater is study that brings to action]
which are clothed in physical things, is in order to refine the sparks of Tohu that fell into the broken vessels
[which are great lights,
in quantity and quality],
and through this aspect of refinement, through this they inherit the Chochmah, Binah, and Daas of Tohu,
and because this is not according to the measure of the refinement, etc.
[and as is known, the refinement now is only in the seven lower sefiros of Tohu, and through this they inherit automatically also the Chochmah, Binah, and Daas of Tohu,
as explained in the continuation of the discourse "Al Tetzar es Moav" of the Mitteler Rebbe]
therefore it is called inheritance.

And when one merits to come to this inheritance, then they give him a gift, meaning that there is drawn from Ein Sof a level above Tohu, which is the aspect of a gift, meaning what is impossible to attain at all except by way of a gift alone.

And this is that it is above inheritance, for although even inheritance is not what one earns through his toil, nevertheless it has a connection, for why does a son inherit from his father? Because he comes from him, etc.
Behold, the matter of inheritance comes to one who has a connection, bond, and relation with him, etc.
And similarly it will be understood in the analogy, that according to his refining the sparks of Tohu
[he becomes an aspect of "brother for good" to Esav]
therefore they give him by way of inheritance the aspect of the lights of Chochmah, Binah, and Daas of Tohu, etc.
But the matter of a gift is what does not come through his action at all, etc.
And in the analogy, it is... that which no arousal from below reaches there, so the drawing down from there is a gift.
And this is what our Sages said,
"In the first three hours, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah,"
and seemingly it is difficult, for did not our Sages say, "Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"
and therefore there cannot be found a single hour that is free when no one is studying at that time at all,
for there is one who has no leisure during the day and studies at night,
and the main study is during the day, as the statement,
"We are daytime workers,"
and nevertheless they also said,
"Night was not created except for study,"
and thus it is found that all day and all night there is no single hour free when there is not one of Israel who is not studying at that time,
and if so, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,
so what is the meaning of what it says that in the first three hours the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah, etc.
Also, the expression "sits and engages in Torah," what is it, etc.
But the explanation is as above, that what is said "whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"
means that it is drawn according to his toil and work,
and this is the precise meaning of the term "opposite him,"
and this is an aspect within the realm of measurement and limitation.
However, what is said "the first three hours" refers to the drawing down
[which is completely above the realm of measurement and limitation]
that is drawn in the aspect of a gift from above, even not through an arousal from below, etc., and therefore it is said about this "sits,"
similar to the lowering of one who sits
[for when he sits, his head is lowered downward],
and "engages in Torah."
And "first three" refers to the level above the realm of measurement and limitation, similar to the first three sefiros that are brought in the books of Kabbalah everywhere.
And nevertheless, even this level, which is completely above an arousal from below, is drawn through that first there is the toil and inheritance mentioned above
[and this is the matter of "his study in his hand"],
for through this they give him as a gift also this level.
And in general,
behold, this is the general distinction between the revealed aspect of Torah and the inner aspect of Torah.
For the revealed aspect of Torah is the aspect of Torah that comes in measure and limitation,
and as it is stated in the Gemara Menachos,
that it is possible for a person to study the entire Torah,
behold, there is an aspect in Torah that comes in limitation.
And nevertheless it is said,
"It is longer than the measure of the earth and broader than the sea,"
and even more,
"And I was with Him, a nursling, and I was His delight day by day, playing before Him at all times,"
which refers to the aspect of the inner aspect of Torah.
And this is the matter of the aspect of "face" and "back" of Torah,
meaning the aspect of the inner and revealed aspects of Torah,
and the aspect of "face" of Torah also illuminates the aspect of "back."

And from these two aspects of "face" and "back" that are in Torah, there is drawn afterward below, in the souls, the two aspects of "face" and "back," and also that the aspect of "face" of the souls illuminates the aspect of "back."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains why Dovid was punished for calling the Torah "songs," because there is a higher level of Torah beyond songs—the aspect of "delight before Him"—and his punishment of forgetfulness regarding carrying the Ark on the shoulder was measure for measure, as the Ark's tablets unified the aspects of "face" and "back."
section.t: And this is also the explanation of what is said,
"Your statutes were songs to me in the house of my sojourn,"
and our Sages said
that Dovid was punished for this.
And as explained in Likkutei Torah
and in Torah Or
and in many places,
the reason,
that he was punished for calling the Torah "songs" is because although the Torah is in the aspect of "songs,"
nevertheless there is an aspect of Torah above this,
"song,"
and even higher, to no end,
which is the aspect of "delight before Him,"
the aspect of "the song of the Holy One, blessed be He," which is hidden from the eyes of all living,
which is the aspect of the inner aspect of Torah.
And this aspect in Torah,
which is in the aspect of "delight before Him,"
is above all measurement and limitation,
to no end, above the aspect of "songs" of Torah,
but nevertheless it is drawn down also below,
and therefore it was said to Dovid, "You called them songs"
(for he praised the Torah for being songs)
in astonishment,
since in the Torah there is an aspect that is to no end, higher than the aspect of songs,
the aspect of "delight before Him,"
the aspect of "song" and the cantillation notes of the Torah.
And with this it will be understood why he was specifically punished with forgetfulness,
and the forgetfulness was regarding the carrying of the Ark on the shoulder,
for this punishment was measure for measure.
And the explanation is,
the matter of the Ark is that in it were the Tablets, as it is said,
"In the Ark there were only the two Tablets."
And the matter of the Tablets was that there was no division of "face" and "back" in them,
as it is stated in the Yerushalmi
on the verse,
"written on both their sides, from this side and from that side,"
that from every side they could be read,
from their four sides, etc.,
meaning that
(it was entirely "face," and)
there was no division of "face" and "back" in it.
And this is also the matter of the commandment of carrying the Ark on the shoulder,
the purpose of which is to connect the shoulder,
which is the aspect of "back,"
to the Ark,
in order to nullify it through this to the Ark
(in which were the Tablets),
similar to what is in the Tablets that are in the Ark itself,
for although a scroll is written on "face" and "back,"
nevertheless, through the Tablets that are in the Ark, the aspects of "face" and "back"
(that are in the scroll)
become unified until they become one
(the aspect of "face"),
and similarly is the matter of connecting the shoulder to the Ark
(in which are the Tablets).
And from this unification of the aspect of "face" and "back" that is through the Tablets,
one must draw down likewise in the study of Torah,
that the aspect of "back" of Torah
(the revealed aspect of Torah)
be unified with the aspect of "face" within it
(the inner aspect of Torah).
And this is why Dovid was specifically punished with forgetfulness,
for "there is no forgetfulness before the Throne of Your glory,"
from the aspect of the inner aspect, forgetfulness does not apply.
For when a person is immersed
(deeply)
in the inner aspect of his soul in some matter, then it is impossible that he will forget it,
but specifically when his devotion to the matter is in the aspect of "back,"
in the aspect of the "back" of his attention.
Therefore he was punished with forgetfulness,
measure for measure.
Because in the Torah he praised the aspect of "back,"
the aspect of "songs" within it alone.
And therefore the punishment of forgetfulness was in the commandment of carrying the Ark on the shoulder,
because its purpose is that through
(the Tablets that are in)
the Torah, the aspects of "face" and "back"
(that are in the Torah)
become unified in a manner that they are entirely "face,"
as above, "written... from this side and from that side," etc.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The study of Torah must be preceded by "blessing the Torah first," which is the service of prayer, and just as in Torah the "face" illuminates the "back," so too in the preceding service of prayer there must be an aspect of "face" illuminating the "back" in the services of yichuda ila'ah and yichuda tata'ah.
section.t: a)
And behold, the study of Torah must be preceded by
(in the language of the Gemara)
"Bless the Torah first,"
meaning the service of man before the Torah.
This is what Abba Binyamin would pray that his prayer be adjacent to his bed,
for the reason for this is,
as explained by the Alter Rebbe,
so that his study of Torah would be after prayer,
for the prayer before the study of Torah is similar to the matter of "bless the Torah first,"
"bless"
(from the term "drawing down")
in the Torah, etc.
And from this it is understood,
that just as in the Torah,
the aspect of "face" illuminates also the aspect of "back"
(as explained above at length),
so too must it be in the service
(of prayer)
that precedes it,
in the service of yichuda ila'ah and yichuda tata'ah.
